title: Web Languages
summary: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP, Ruby and WebAssembly: the languages of the browser and the server behind it. The event loop is the threshold: until it clicks, asynchronous JavaScript looks like it runs in random order.
sources: Simpson: You Don't Know JS Yet

nodes.label: HTML: Structure & Semantics
nodes.summary: Semantic elements give structure, accessibility and search visibility for free.
nodes.outcome: Mark up a page with semantic, accessible HTML.
nodes.check: Why use <button> instead of a clickable <div>?
nodes.answer: A button is focusable, works with the keyboard and is announced to screen readers by default.

nodes.label: CSS: The Cascade & Layout
nodes.summary: Specificity, source order, flexbox and grid.
nodes.outcome: Lay out a responsive page with grid and flexbox.
nodes.check: Two CSS rules with equal specificity set the same property. Which one wins?
nodes.answer: The one that comes later in the source.

nodes.label: The DOM & Browser APIs
nodes.summary: The page as a live tree of objects that scripts read and change.
nodes.outcome: Update the page from JavaScript through the DOM.
nodes.answer: The browser's tree of objects representing the page, which scripts can read and change.

nodes.label: JavaScript: The Language of the Browser
nodes.summary: Dynamic, prototype-based and everywhere, with historical quirks.
nodes.outcome: Write modern JavaScript with modules and const/let.
nodes.check: What does typeof null return in JavaScript?

nodes.label: "== and === are the same"
nodes.summary: == coerces types before comparing; === does not.
nodes.outcome: Use strict equality and predict coercion.
nodes.answer: true for == (type coercion) and false for === (strict equality).

nodes.label: JavaScript: The Event Loop & Async
nodes.summary: One thread, a call stack and queues of tasks and microtasks; promises and async/await sit on top.
nodes.outcome: Predict the output order of mixed sync, timer and promise code.
nodes.check: setTimeout(f, 0) is called, then console.log('a'). Which runs first, f or the log?
nodes.answer: The log: f waits in the task queue until the current code finishes.

nodes.label: TypeScript: Types for JavaScript
nodes.summary: Static types checked at compile time, erased in the JavaScript output.
nodes.outcome: Type a JavaScript module with TypeScript.
nodes.check: Do TypeScript's types exist at run time in the browser?
nodes.answer: No: types are erased when compiling to JavaScript; checking happens at compile time.

nodes.label: PHP: Server-Side Web
nodes.summary: Runs on the server per request; powers a large share of the web.
nodes.outcome: Render a page from a PHP template with escaped output.
nodes.check: Where does PHP code run: in the browser or on the server?
nodes.answer: On the server; the browser receives the HTML it produces.

nodes.label: Ruby & Rails
nodes.summary: An expressive language and a framework built on convention over configuration.
nodes.outcome: Scaffold a CRUD app in Rails.
nodes.check: What does 'convention over configuration' mean in Rails?
nodes.answer: Following naming and folder conventions means you write little configuration; Rails infers the wiring.

nodes.label: WebAssembly
nodes.summary: A portable bytecode that runs compiled C++, Rust and Go in the browser.
nodes.outcome: Compile a function to WebAssembly and call it from JavaScript.
nodes.check: Why compile C++ or Rust to WebAssembly?
nodes.answer: To run near-native-speed code in the browser, sandboxed alongside JavaScript.
